labels.text: `agi mcp list` shows the registered names.

S55.04.needs: a registered MCP server (agi mcp add first)
S55.04.note: The detail view shows only name, status, transport, target, file and rules. The CLI has no connector detail page with description, publisher or links.
steps: Type agi mcp list to see the registered server names.
Type agi mcp get <name> with one of those names.
Look at the lines name, status, transport, target and file, and compare them with Expected. The description, publisher, sign-in requirement, tools and links are not shown here.
S55.04.where: agi mcp list, then agi mcp get <name>

S55.05.needs: a registered MCP server; /mcp tools lists only servers connected in this session
steps: Type agi mcp get <name> in a terminal.
Look for the Tools (N): list with each tool name and description.
Start agi, type /mcp tools and look for the MCP tools: list.
S55.05.where: agi mcp get <name>, or /mcp tools [server] inside an agi session

labels.text: The token is stored in the OS credential store.
Connect one in your browser, for example

S55.07.needs: a remote server address, a browser, and an outside account for that service
S55.07.note: There is no in-app Connect button. Connecting is a command plus a browser step, and login needs an interactive terminal.
steps: Type agi mcp add <name> --url <https address> to register a remote server.
Type agi mcp login <name> in an interactive terminal and complete the step in the browser.
Look for The token is stored in the OS credential store. For account connectors, run agi connectors and look for Connect one in your browser.
S55.07.where: agi mcp login <name> (remote server); for account connectors, agi connectors shows the browser address to connect

labels.text: The token is stored in the OS credential store.

S55.08.needs: an account at an OAuth provider and a browser
S55.08.note: Login requires an interactive terminal; the code says it needs one to open the browser.
steps: Register an OAuth remote server with agi mcp add <name> --url <https URL>.
Type agi mcp login <name>; the provider consent page should open in the browser.
Approve access in the browser, then look in the terminal for The token is stored in the OS credential store.
Type agi mcp get <name> and check that it lists tools.

labels.text: Header for a remote server as "Name: value", for example an API key. Repeat for each.

S55.09.needs: the API key for the service
S55.09.note: There is no entry form; the key is typed as a header flag. Encryption of the stored key was not checked.
steps: Type agi mcp add <name> --url <https URL> --header "<Header name>: <your API key>".
Press Enter and read the success line the command prints.
Type agi mcp get <name> and check that it connects and lists tools.

S55.18.needs: at least one registered MCP server or a connected account connector
S55.18.note: Account connectors show health text only when it is not healthy.
steps: Start agi and type /mcp.
Read the status after each server name: connected, disabled, needs authentication, failed, blocked by your workspace or starting.
Type /mcp info <server> and look for responding or not responding.
Type agi connectors and look for needs reconnecting or connected since <date>, <health>.
S55.18.where: /mcp inside an agi session; /mcp info <server>; agi connectors for account connectors

S55.20.needs: an account connector whose connection expired or was revoked, or a remote MCP server that needs sign-in
S55.20.note: There is no Reconnect button in the CLI. The CLI prints a URL to open.
steps: Type agi connectors.
Find a connector that shows needs reconnecting: open <url>.
Open that URL in the browser and reconnect, then run agi connectors again.
Look for connected since on that connector. For an MCP server showing needs authentication, run agi mcp login <name>.
S55.20.where: agi connectors (account connectors); agi mcp login <name> (remote MCP servers)

S55.21.note: /mcp test runs the same reconnect as /mcp restart and takes no server name.
steps: Type agi mcp get <name> in a terminal.
Look at the connection line: could not connect with a reason, or did not answer within 20 seconds, or the server name and Tools list when it works.
Start agi, type /mcp restart and look for MCP reconnected: N tool(s) available. or MCP restart failed.
S55.21.where: agi mcp get <name>; /mcp restart inside an agi session

labels.text: Its saved sign-in and tool permissions are removed

S55.22.needs: a connector connected to your account
S55.22.note: Removing an MCP server with agi mcp remove is a separate path from disconnecting an account connector.
steps: Type agi connectors and note the connector id.
Type agi connectors disconnect <id>, read the prompt and its consequence, then answer it.
Look for Disconnected <id> from your account.
Type agi connectors again and ask the assistant to use that connector; check that it is no longer offered.
S55.22.where: agi connectors disconnect <connector> (account connectors); agi mcp remove <name> (MCP servers)

S55.23.needs: a remote MCP server signed in over OAuth, and the provider account
S55.23.note: Account connectors have only disconnect in the CLI, with no separate revoke.
steps: Use a remote server already signed in with agi mcp login <name>.
Type agi mcp logout <name>.
Look for Revoked the OAuth grant for '<name>' at its provider and removed the stored token.
If the provider did not confirm, read the line that tells you to remove the app's access in the provider's own settings, and check that page.

S55.27.needs: a registered MCP server; a Managed session to see workspace rules
S55.27.note: The CLI sets rules per server or per tool. A read and write split exists only in the workspace policy.
steps: Type agi mcp block <server> <tool>; look for the message that says the tool is now blocked.
Type agi mcp get <server> and look for the rule line showing blocked, asks first or runs without asking.
Type agi mcp unset <server> <tool> to remove the setting.
In a Managed session type /connectors and look for the Workspace connectors section; write tools rules there are set by the workspace, not here.
S55.27.where: agi mcp ask|allow|block <server> [tool] to set it; agi mcp get <server> to view it; /connectors shows workspace tool rules

S55.29.needs: a connector that supplied data in an answer
S55.29.note: Searched apps/cli/src for attribution and provider text near answers and tool output. Only the approval prompt Allow MCP tool '<tool>' from server '<server>'? (agent/tools.rs:150) names a server; no provider label on answers was found.

S55.30.needs: a remote MCP server whose tool needs a scope your grant lacks; hard to set up
S55.30.note: The product prints the instruction in the error. It does not show a grant prompt inside the session.
steps: Use a remote server whose tool needs a wider permission than your grant.
Ask the assistant to run that tool.
Look for the error text needs the additional permission '<scope>'. Run agi mcp login <name> to grant it.
Type agi mcp login <name>, approve in the browser, then ask again and check that the tool runs.
S55.30.where: agi mcp login <name>, after a tool error in an agi session

S55.32.needs: a service on a private network
S55.32.note: Searched apps/cli/src for private network, VPN and tunnel. Only refusals for private addresses in fetch tools (features/exec/tools/mod.rs:1523, permissions.rs:173) were found; validate_remote_url in mcp/registry.rs accepts only http and https. No private-network setup was found.
